title: Multijurisdictional legal-hold and residency sync with Seabright Trust
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO evidence pack + regional deployment diagram (Samira) - by 2027-11-30
Schedule 1hr SE-led private deployment scoping session to validate HSM/KMS integration (Daniel + Marco) - week of 2027-12-06
Customer to provide list of data flows requiring legal-hold / e-discovery and sensitive buckets (Priya) - by 2027-12-02
action_items: Samira: send security whitepaper and link to benchmark spreadsheet (due 2027-11-30)
Daniel: prepare architecture sketch for VPC/private control plane with HSM integration (due 2027-12-04)
Marco: extract sample retention policy and legal-hold scenarios and share with Redwood (due 2027-12-02)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-25 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lena Morales (Seabright Security), Tom Erikson (Platform), Priya Shah (Legal Ops), Marco (SRE)
Links shared: security-deck.pdf, regional-hosting-diagram.png, benchmark-latency-spreadsheet.xlsx

Summary: initial residency + legal-hold discovery across EU/US/CH subsidiaries, focus on audit evidence, KMS/HSM residency, log redaction and retention, and whether hosted vs dedicated vs private fulfills legal-hold/ediscovery constraints.

00:00:00 Samira: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 50 minutes, we'll do quick intros then jump into the residency and legal hold scenarios you sent over.
00:00:12 Lena: thanks, yeah from security i'm lena, i'm primarily worried about cross-border copy of personal data and the ability to enforce legal holds when regulators request records.
00:00:22 Tom: tom here, platform. we run services in eu-west-1 and central-us, and we have a swiss subsidiary that requires data not to leave ch region, at least for certain datasets.
00:00:35 Daniel: cool. quick context: Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and a private control plane deployment in customer VPC or on-prem. we often see a split where low risk models live in hosted, but regulated traffic goes to dedicated or private.
00:00:51 Priya: right, our legal ops need to model legal-hold across subsidiaries. curious - if we use hosted, do you ever replicate logs or content to us outside region for debugging?
00:01:04 Samira: good question. hosted by default keeps control plane meta logs in primary region; we can configure regional retention and also opt for region-locking. diagnostics traces used for support are redacted and require customer approval to pull. but i'll let daniel add the technical nuance.
00:01:20 Daniel: yes, and to add, for hosted we have limited region-lock guarantees; for strict residency we recommend dedicated or private. dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool in region X, but the control plane still is Redwood-managed unless you choose private. private control plane can be deployed into your VPC so nothing leaves your network except the model artifacts you allow.
00:01:40 Lena: and about logs - we need full audit trails for model inputs/outputs for certain investigations but with the ability to redact or minimize PII for normal retention. is that something you support?
00:01:53 Daniel: we support token-level redaction and configurable retention windows. also we offer log minimization where sensitive fields are replaced at the edge prior to ingestion. caveat: that affects debugging fidelity so we recommend a canary path where redacted logs are default and full logs are kept only in app-specific legal-hold buckets.
00:02:13 Tom: how do you manage KMS keys? our compliance requires customer-managed keys that reside in EU or CH for certain data classes.
00:02:23 Daniel: we integrate with cloud KMS and also with HSM-backed key stores for private deployments. for hosted, we offer CMK where the key is customer-managed but in Redwood's KMS tenant; for private, the keys can be in your KMS/HSM inside your VPC, so full control.
00:02:38 Lena: any support for key escrow or regulator-mandated key access? we've had auditors ask about escrow for Swiss entities.
00:02:47 Samira: we have a few enterprise setups with controlled key-escrow workflows; it's typically part of an enterprise contract and involves defined access procedures, dual controls, and often a legal agreement. we'll need to engage legal if you want that modeled.
00:03:02 Priya: noted. can you describe evidence collection for SOC2/ISO audits? what do we get out of the box?
00:03:10 Daniel: out-of-box you get audit logs for admin actions, model deployments, and access logs. for dedicated/private customers we can provide enriched evidence packages: signed attestations, infrastructure diagrams, and runbooks. we can also provide per-account artifact exports for audit purposes.
00:03:30 Tom: about legal-hold specifically: if regulator asks to preserve messages generated by the model, are those stored in the same storage tier as logs or is there a separate immutable archive?
00:03:41 Daniel: we support immutable archives (WORM-style) for legal-hold exports. you can configure retention and make exports immutable. for hosted, that archive may be in a Redwood-controlled region unless you push exports to your own bucket. for private, the archive sits in your environment.
00:03:59 Lena: so in practice you'd recommend private for swiss-only data?
00:04:05 Samira: yes for the strictest residency and control. dedicated can be configured in region with customer-only access, but the control plane still touches metadata. private is the gold standard for isolation and compliance.
00:04:17 Marco: operational question - how do upgrades/rollouts work in private? we patch and upgrade on our change windows, regulators want evidence of the patch timeline.
00:04:26 Daniel: upgrades are coordinated. in private we provide an upgrade channel and you can choose staged rollouts; we produce a timeline and release notes and can sign change logs for audit.
00:04:37 Priya: cross-border e-discovery: when we run a search for records subject to a legal hold, is there tooling to scope by country/subsidiary?
00:04:48 Daniel: yes we have filters by tenant, model, and region tag; for private you can restrict search to local storage only. hosted gives you tagging but the export path might be routed via Redwood's control plane unless you use customer-bucket exports.
00:05:03 Samira: quick poll - is data residency a 'must have' or a 'nice to have' for the pilot?
00:05:10 Tom: must have for Swiss PII and EU financial data. for US-only test workloads it's nice to have but not blocking.
00:05:19 Lena: and we also have a requirement to minimize logs for analytics team - retention 30 days default, but legal-hold items can be pulled to a 7-year archive.
00:05:29 Daniel: okay. we'll sketch an architecture with regional retention and a legal-hold export path to a customer-owned bucket that triggers an immutable archive.
00:05:40 00:05:40 Speaker 1: [inaudible] excuse me, quick side question, latency impact if we run private with on-prem GPUs?
00:05:50 Daniel: if on-prem GPUs are in your network, latency is best case; the tradeoff is our hosted autoscaling and multi-region fallbacks aren't available unless you federate. so cost and elasticity differ.
00:06:04 Tom: right, we worry about throughput during month-end batch jobs and whether private can autoscale.
00:06:11 Daniel: private supports autoscaling with your infra if you configure a scaling controller; Redwood provides policies but it uses your capacity. dedicated has built-in autoscale within the reserved pool boundaries.
00:06:24 Priya: about regulatory holds - can we do targeted retention on a per-customer or per-contract basis? e.g., clients in bank A have 7-year hold, others 3-year.
00:06:35 Daniel: yes, retention policies are policy-driven and can be scoped to namespaces/tenants/labels. you can also attach legal-hold flags that override retention.
00:06:45 Lena: for forensic access we need an audit trail showing who accessed what, when, and why. do you provide attestation logs that are cryptographically signed?
00:06:56 Daniel: we provide signed audit logs for enterprise plans; they include hashes and can be fed into your SIEM. again for private we can localize that entirely to your logging pipeline.
00:07:08 Samira: i'm noting a few follow-ups: a patch and release proof doc, a KMS/HSM integration sketch, and a legal-hold export process. we'll include the SOC2 evidence pack.
00:07:18 00:07:18 Tom: another nuance: subsidiary in CH requires notifications to regulator before any cross-border transfer. will Redwood's hosted model ever push data cross-border for model improvements or telemetry?
00:07:32 Samira: we do not use customer prompts for model training unless explicitly opted-in; telemetry is aggregated and can be disabled for enterprise agreements. cross-border telemetry can be disabled too.
00:07:44 Priya: i saw in docs mention of "KV cache" being trimmed - any chance that cache could contain PII? what's policy for cache flushing?
00:07:54 Daniel: KV cache holds ephemeral context and is encrypted in transit and at rest; default TTLs are short but some workloads extend the cache for session continuity. for regulated data we recommend cache isolation or disabling KV cache when PII can't be stored.
00:08:09 Marco: okay. for the pilot timeline we want to run a small POC that simulates a legal-hold export. what would you need from us?
00:08:18 Daniel: a sample dataset, list of retention rules, and the regulatory scenarios you want tested. we'll run the POC in a dedicated region or private environment depending on the control you need.
00:08:28 Lena: sample dataset must include synthetic PII mirroring production patterns and a list of e-discovery queries.
00:08:35 Samira: we'll also include a playbook doc for the POC.
00:08:40 00:08:40 Speaker 2: [crosstalk] can i just say, vendor lock-in concern: if we start in hosted then later shift to private, how easy is migration?
00:08:50 Daniel: model artifacts and prompts are exportable; we version models and you can pin a model in a private deployment. biggest work is infrastructure provisioning and KMS key migration, but we have migration guides for that.
00:09:04 Priya: what about legal holds across subsidiaries when data resides in multiple regions - is there a single API to trigger a hold everywhere?
00:09:13 Daniel: we provide a legal-hold API that can target all tenants and regions; for hosted it triggers Redwood-managed exports, for private it's an API that triggers your local pipelines. we'll show the API contract in the follow-up.
00:09:27 Tom: can we scope holds by model invocation type? e.g., assistant responses vs. embeddings.
00:09:35 Daniel: yes, scoping can be by route/model/input type. embeddings are treated as derivative metadata and may need separate handling.
00:09:44 Lena: any standard redaction helpers? e.g., PII detectors that can be applied pre-ingest?
00:09:52 Daniel: we have a PII detection hook and can apply redaction or token mapping at the SDK/edge layer. there are some false positives so we recommend human-in-the-loop for legal-hold validations.
00:10:06 00:10:06 Priya: about evidence retention - regulators sometimes want chain of custody. how do you show custody over exported records?
00:10:16 Daniel: exports are signed, timestamped, and include hash chains. for private, everything is under your custody. for hosted we can provide signed attestations.
00:10:27 Tom: do you support e-discovery integrations (e.g., Relativity or other tools) or do we need to build the connector?
00:10:35 Daniel: we have S3/gs-compatible export formats; many customers build connectors to their e-discovery tools. we can help scope a connector in the POC.
00:10:45 Samira: shifting to a quick run of the sample scenarios you sent — lena, you listed three: swiss-only PII, eu-financial records, and global non-sensitive logs. can we walk through the swiss-only flow?
00:10:58 Lena: sure. for swiss-only, the dataset must never leave CH region, keys must be in CH HSM, and any export for regulator must be delivered to CH-located legal team.
00:11:09 Daniel: for that we'd propose a private control plane deployed in CH VPC with compute either in CH or on-prem. KMS in CH HSM, log retention and WORM archive in CH bucket. all admin access restricted via SAML SSO to your CH admin group.
00:11:27 Priya: and if a regulator asks for immediate snapshot, can we get an immutable snapshot within X hours?
00:11:34 Daniel: yes, the legal-hold export path can be automated; typical SLA we see is 24-48 hours for a full export, faster for scoped snapshots. we can agree to a tighter SLA in contract.
00:11:46 Marco: operationally, who can trigger that export? role-based access?
00:11:51 Daniel: RBAC supports roles and approvals; you can require two-person approval for legal-hold exports. logs of approvals are stored with the export.
00:11:59 00:11:59 Speaker 1: [quiet] what's the cost implication for keeping long-term immutable archives in-region?
00:12:06 Samira: cost is mostly storage + retrieval and the administrative overhead; private deployments avoid cross-region egress costs but require your infra spend for compute. we'll include a TCO sketch in the follow-up.
00:12:18 Lena: is there any feature that can reduce retention costs, like summaries or hashed derivatives?
00:12:24 Daniel: yes, for analytics you can store hashed or vectorized derivatives (embeddings) instead of raw content; embeddings are smaller but they carry risk if re-identification is possible, so treat them as sensitive where applicable.
00:12:39 Priya: legal question: will Redwood sign a data processing addendum (DPA) that includes regional restrictions?
00:12:46 Samira: standard is yes; enterprise contracts include DPAs with region clauses. we'll provide a template DPA for review.
00:12:53 Tom: on the security list, we need for our auditors proof of disaster recovery for private control plane - how is DR handled?
00:13:01 Daniel: DR for private is typically customer-managed; we recommend cross-az replication for critical components and a warm standby region option. Redwood can provide runbooks and test evidence.
00:13:12 00:13:12 Marco: one more technical detail: model rollback - if a model produces regressive outputs and we need to freeze a dataset, can we freeze rollout and revert?
00:13:20 Daniel: yes, model pinning and rollback is supported; we keep deployment history and can rollback to prior stable versions.
00:13:27 Lena: okay, i want to raise an odd case: legal-hold on embeddings derived from PII — how do you prove deletion? because embeddings are irreversible but can be reidentified sometimes.
00:13:40 Daniel: we treat embeddings as persistent derivatives; deletion requires scrubbing the vector store and any backups. we provide deletion proof but you should consider not storing embeddings for regulated subjects or using a transient store.
00:13:55 Priya: would you support a pattern where embeddings are computed in a customer enclave and only hashed tokens are sent to Redwood?
00:14:04 Daniel: yes, that's a pattern some customers use: client-side featurization, then only non-PII vectors land in Redwood. we can support via private connectors.
00:14:13 00:14:13 Speaker 2: [laughter] someone's dog barked in background
00:14:16 Samira: happens to all of us. ok switching gears - compliance evidence: we'll attach our SOC2 report and ISO summary, but auditors sometimes ask for application-level logs. can you confirm what admin-level logs include?
00:14:29 Daniel: admin logs include user provisioning, role changes, API key creation, model deploys, config changes. we can export logs in a friendly CSV/JSON for ingestion to your SIEM.
00:14:40 Tom: do you capture content-level logs by default for admin? we want strict separation where infra admins can't see user content unless approved.
00:14:50 Daniel: separation is enforced: infra/admin logs show metadata, not raw content. content access requires additional role and an approval workflow.
00:14:59 Lena: i noticed some customers ask for 'redaction at edge' SDK. does Redwood provide SDK hooks for pre-ingest redaction?
00:15:08 Daniel: yes, SDKs have middleware hooks for redaction, PII masking, and tokenization. we also provide sample patterns.
00:15:17 00:15:17 Priya: fine, i'm going to ask about long term legal holds - if we export to our bucket and then delete in Redwood, can we keep a sealed copy that only legal ops can unseal?
00:15:29 Daniel: you can implement a sealed bucket with encryption keys only legal ops holds; Redwood can orchestrate the export but custody is with you. for additional seals we can sign the export.
00:15:40 Marco: on monitoring - can we get token-level cost and latency per route for compliance reporting?
00:15:47 Samira: yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdown. we can generate route-specific reports.
00:15:55 Daniel: and for dedicated/private we provide telemetry endpoints you can ship to your observability stack.
00:16:03 00:16:03 Tom: any gotchas about backups - if we run private, do automatic backups ever cross region?
00:16:10 Daniel: not unless you configure cross-region replication. default is local snapshots. cross-region replication is opt-in and documented.
00:16:19 Lena: we also have a regulator requirement for SSO with audit logging - SAML or OIDC?
00:16:25 Daniel: both supported; SAML is common for enterprises and we log SSO events.
00:16:31 Priya: for the POC could you include a demo of a legal-hold export and a mock regulator request?
00:16:37 Samira: yes we'll do that in the SE scoping session.
00:16:41 00:16:41 Speaker 1: [typing] what about backup retention policy for deleted records - do you have a secure purge process?
00:16:50 Daniel: secure purge is supported with audit trail; deletions can cascade and we can provide deletion manifests for proof.
00:16:58 Tom: wonderful. i want to discuss SLA for response on preservation requests - can we get an uptime and response SLA?
00:17:06 Samira: enterprise plans include SLA for availability; preservation response SLA is contract-negotiated. we'll propose a 24-hour acknowledgement and 72-hour full export in the draft.
00:17:17 Lena: curious about pen tests and external audits — do you provide scope for us to rely on your pen tests?
00:17:24 Samira: yes we share high-level pen test summaries and remediation reports for enterprise customers under NDA.
00:17:31 00:17:31 Marco: how granular are RBAC perms? can we make a role that only triggers legal-hold exports and nothing else?
00:17:40 Daniel: yes role-based permissions are very granular. you can create a role with single permission to trigger exports and another to approve.
00:17:50 Priya: any concerns with data subject access requests (DSARs) using the API?
00:17:56 Daniel: DSARs are handled via export APIs; we can help automate workflows to pull subject-specific data and redact as needed.
00:18:06 Samira: quick checkpoint - i'll share the DPA and SOC2 pack, daniel will scope the private architecture and the POC steps.
00:18:14 00:18:14 Tom: ok let's go into the eu-financial scenario briefly - that one requires encryption keys in eu, and auditors want signed access logs for 5 years.
00:18:24 Daniel: for that we'd recommend dedicated in EU region with CMK in your KMS and signed audit logs forwarded to your archive. retention and WORM policies can be applied.
00:18:34 Lena: do you have any customers doing multi-tenant legal-hold by contract? we're curious about pattern.
00:18:41 Daniel: yes, our namespace model maps to contracts; many customers apply retention per-contract and flag legal-hold at that level.
00:18:49 Priya: okay last - procurement timeline. we aim to decide by mid-december, any blockers?
00:18:56 Samira: none from our side; primary blockers are proof-of-concept results and legal review of DPA. we'll accelerate the SE scoping and send materials this week.
00:19:07 00:19:07 Speaker 2: [brief static] small echo on call
00:19:10 Marco: since we've been talking a lot - can you show a sample of the legal-hold API contract in the follow-up?
00:19:16 Daniel: yes we'll include an API spec with examples.
00:19:21 Samira: any other concerns we haven't covered?
00:19:25 Lena: one edge case - if we need to perform partial anonymization for analytics but keep traces for audit, do you support separate retention policies per field?
00:19:36 Daniel: you can have per-field redaction and retention in the pre-ingest layer; again that's where the SDK middleware helps.
00:19:44 Priya: from legal ops, we'll compile a checklist of must-haves and a mapping to Redwood features. expect that by Dec 2.
00:19:53 Samira: great. we'll send the SOC2/ISO pack, the DPA template, the architecture sketches, and propose times for the SE scoping session.
00:20:02 00:20:02 Speaker 1: thanks all.
00:20:05 Samira: thanks, we'll wrap with a recap - action items in the notes.
00:20:09 Transcript notes: some transcription noise around 00:08 and 00:19, occasional mis-attributed speaker lines.

End of transcript.
